The Court Made The Following:
 Order
1.

The petitioner is sought to be prosecuted for the offences punishable under Sections 306, 114 R/w Section 34 of IPC.
2.

Accused No.1, who is the wife of the deceased used to frequently quarrel with the deceased by threatening him to provide luxurious life and also provide a separate home and accused No.2 instigated accused No.1 to do the same.
Unable to bear the harassment, the deceased moved to a rented house and unable to pay the rent, the deceased informed his mother that he intends to die.
He further informed on phone that the harassment meted out by accused Nos.1 and 2 has increased.
NC: 2023:KHC-K:1294 Unable to bear the harassment meted out
, the son of the informant committed suicide on 11.05.2019.
3. The police after investigation, submitted the charge sheet for the aforesaid offences.

sentences.text: 2 4. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1- State.
5. Respondent No.2-De-facto complainant is reported to be dead.
Hence, the petition as against respondent No.2 is dismissed as abated.

6. To constitute an offence punishable under Sections 306 of IPC and 107 of IPC, the intention of the accused to aid or instigate or abet the deceased to commit suicide is necessary and there must be a clear mens rea to commit the offence and it also requires an active act or direct act which lead the deceased to commit suicide seeing no option and this act must have been intended to push the deceased into such a position that he committed suicide.
7.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar reported in (2022)
6 SCC 599, at para 18 has held as follows:
"18.

entities.text:
Kahkashan Kausar v. State of Bihar reported in (2022)
6 SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate that this court has at numerous instances expressed NC: 2023:KHC-K:1294 concern over the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial disputes, without analysing the long term ramifications of a trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further manifest from the said judgments that false implication by way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse of the process of law.

Therefore, this court by way of its judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie case is made out against them."
8.

In the present case, except the allegation that accused No.1 at the instigation of accused No.2 used to quarrel with her husband to provide luxurious life, and also a separate home, there is no allegation that there was a clear mens rea on the part of the accused to commit the offence.

Hence,
in the absence of essential ingredients so as to constitute the commission of the aforesaid offence,
the continuation of the criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i. Criminal petition is allowed.
ii. The impugned proceedings in S.C.No.50/2021, pending on the file of II Addl.
District and Sessions Judge at Raichur, arising out of Crime No.59/2019, NC:
2023:KHC-K:1294 registered by Sindhanur Town Police Station, for the offences punishable under Sections 306, 114 R/w Section 34 of IPC is hereby quashed.
iii.
